newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat ignore surprise EU refund hike.
newsitem.headline: French wheat ignore surprise EU refund hike.

text.p: An overnight fall in U.S wheat futures cancelled the positive impact on French wheat prices of a surprise hike in the European Union's (EU) wheat export subsidy, dealers said on Friday.
Wheat into Rouen for November-December delivery was paid at 855 francs per tonne, after quoting at 855-860 francs on Thursday.
On Thursday the EU nearly doubled to 13 Ecus per tonne the aid given to wheat exports to keep pace with falling world prices.
Chicago futures tumbled on the news, closing 11-1/2 to 14 1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 14-1/2 at $3.84.
Traders said while the surprise refund hike was a step in the right direction, higher refunds were needed to help exporters face fierce competition on world grain markets.
"Yesterday's award was a surprise that leads to a greater optimism. But this must be continued," one dealer said.
"A refund of 13 Ecus is good but we need 20 Ecus to export," another trader said
Dealers will also be closely monitoring the outcome of a tender Egypt has launched for the import of 50,000 tonnes of French or Australian soft wheat.
The results of the tender are expected later on Friday.
Some traders were already speculating Egypt may buy more wheat than it initially tendered for.
